extensions.scope: Mission Control and Dashboard / Defense Workspace; preserve their distinct overview and record-oriented layouts.

motion.name: scene-overlay
motion.value: segmented rotating rings; comet trails; pulsing beacons; cyan scan beam
motion.purpose: Mission Control only. Decorative Three.js effects aligned to contained artwork; raster image stays static.

motion.name: meter
motion.purpose: Metric bar updates; no transition under reduced motion.

motion.name: overlay-render-limit
motion.value: 33ms minimum frame interval; DPR <= 1.5; elapsed-time clock
motion.purpose: Mission Control only. Pause/resume without timeline jumps; stop frame loop while hidden or offscreen.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: autoplay at .35 elapsed-time speed; explicit Play/Pause control
motion.purpose: Mission Control only. Current Mission scene behavior; reduced-motion CSS disables scene/meter transitions and smooth scrolling.

motion.name: overlay-lifecycle
motion.value: persisted pagehide suspends; persisted pageshow resizes and restarts; noncached pagehide disposes
motion.purpose: Mission Control only. Preserve GPU resources across BFCache navigation and release them on noncached navigation.

motion.name: static-fallback
motion.value: static raster; visible disabled Animation unavailable control
motion.purpose: Mission Control only. Preserve the artwork on Three.js/WebGL failure or context loss; restoration re-enables the control.

narrative.overview:
Mission Control is a dense midnight-navy operations console with a cyan illuminated center. The supplied dashboard reference governs this built surface: compact incident evidence frames a large shield/world composition, while restrained neural imagery supports the AI status stack.

This system applies to Mission Control and the authorized Dashboard extension (Defense Workspace). Mission keeps its three-column overview; Dashboard reuses the palette, local fonts and shield artwork as a static decorative page background while giving operational records the primary reading space. Small English condensed headings and numerals pair with readable Thai and English operational copy; measured borders and tonal panels keep the artwork from competing with evidence.
keyCharacteristics: Dense operational hierarchy with a dominant central scene.
Local bilingual fonts, thin cyan line icons and tabular metrics.
Generated 3D raster art with restrained decorative Three.js overlays.
Visible sample scope, sensor coverage and human approval state.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: Every health or severity color must have a readable status, count or category beside it.

rules.name: The Quiet Frame Rule
rules.body: Keep panels flat and borders restrained; reserve luminous depth for the generated art and its decorative overlay.

dos: Do keep sensor coverage and sample scope adjacent to their metrics.
Do use the central raster artwork as the static visual foundation.
Do preserve the mobile reading order: visibility, scene and metrics, incidents, then AI and health.
Do keep keyboard focus visible and state labels readable without color.
donts: Don't let the static 3D background dominate Dashboard records or obscure capture limitations.
Don't present decorative world paths as attacker geolocation.
Don't turn a green gateway state into a claim of automatic enforcement or complete network coverage.
Don't invent compliance badges, endpoint inventories or totals beyond the loaded sample.
